evidence: Cato Agr. 14: quae opus sunt dominus praebēbit
terms.comment: With the dative of the person provided for: alicui aliquid praebēre. Things provide too: quae praebet lātās arbor spatiantibus umbrās, the tree that gives wide shade to those who walk under it (Ov. Rem. 85).

terms.gloss: supply in plenty; be on hand
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.12: ea, quae suppeditent ad cultum et ad victum
terms.comment: Transitive, to supply; intransitive, of things that are there in plenty.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.62: īnstruere et parāre convīvium omnibus rēbus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of fitting out a house or a meal with everything needed.

phrases.english: roof tiles were provided at public expense

phrases.latin: hae reī māteriem et quae opus sunt dominus praebēbit
phrases.english: for this work the owner will provide the timber and whatever is needed
to supply someone with men and arms
